rungs.title: Person masks and per-view identity
rungs.status: measured (surface): ours 0.52-0.63 IoU, oracle 0.71-0.88, recall falls twice as far as precision

visuals.title: D3: how well the delivered outline covers the person in the footage, before and after
visuals.plain: MAMMA's person masks are the reference; higher is better. This is the instrument that FELL under D2b. It rose in all eight cells once the mesh carried the same skeleton the joints were solved on. The hatched bar is MAMMA's own mesh through the same rasteriser.

visuals.title: What D2 cost on the photographs: outline overlap before and after
visuals.plain: Each camera's own person mask is the reference, the one measurement here that reads pixels of the footage rather than another model. The skeleton is better placed by every joint measure and the mesh bound to it overlaps worse; the discordance lives in what joins them. MAMMA's mesh through the same renderer is the ceiling.

visuals.title: How much our body outline overlaps the person in the frame
visuals.plain: Each camera's own person mask is the reference. MAMMA's mesh through the same renderer is the best this measurement can reach; a flat rectangle over the person is the wrong answer that must lose.

bars.label: MAMMA's pose on an average body
A flat rectangle over the person

visuals.title: How much of the person our outline covers (recall)
visuals.plain: Ours falls twice as far below MAMMA on recall as on precision: the delivered body is too small and misplaced rather than too big.

rungs.title: 2D landmarks
rungs.status: measured with controls; the coherent bias is ~11 px at 3840, not 18.6, and the verdict is the pseudo-label campaign

visuals.title: Detector error after triangulation, and how much a coordinate fix could remove
visuals.plain: MAMMA's fitted joints are the reference, at zero. The first bar is our detector as it is; the second is after the best honest per-camera shift; the third is the ceiling no shift can beat. Most of the error is per-joint, which is why the next step is training, not offsets.

visuals.title: How well the four cameras agree with each other about our detector's points
visuals.plain: No reference at all: the detector against itself across views. Pairing the wrong people across cameras must score far worse, and it does.

visuals.title: Times the two performers were confused for each other
visuals.plain: MAMMA's subject labels are the reference. Zero is the target, and it must still hold when one camera runs a frame early or late.

Ours, one camera a frame late

visuals.title: Our triangulation given MAMMA's own 2D points
visuals.plain: MAMMA's exact landmarks are the reference. About 10 mm is the floor the reference itself imposes, so these bars say our geometry reaches it.

rungs.title: Temporal solve and smoothing
rungs.status: measured on synthetic truth (I2, I7): 1.15 mm floor; the solve beats a line 6.7x on burst outages and loses on isolated drops; zero-phase smoother

visuals.title: Our whole pipeline on a perfect detector: how far from the truth it lands
visuals.plain: MAMMA's skeleton projected into the cameras is the exact truth here. The floor is about one millimetre and all of it is the smoothing stage; a rig one frame out of sync costs six times that.

visuals.title: What happens to a joint when only one camera can still see it
visuals.plain: MAMMA's own skeleton projected into the four cameras is the exact truth here, so every millimetre is our reconstruction's. When a joint is lost for a run of frames the sequence solve lands nearly seven times closer than drawing a line through the gap. When the loss is a single isolated frame the line wins instead; the figures below the chart carry that arm.

visuals.title: What the smoothing window does to a bad detection
visuals.plain: Exact truth from our own motion clips, no MAMMA anywhere in this chart. One landmark is thrown off by as much as our own detector's worst 1%; the shipped 300 ms window removes most of the damage, and removing the window leaves it.

visuals.title: D3: does the delivered character carry the body the joints were solved on?
visuals.plain: The reference is the track's own forward kinematics, so the right answer is zero. The hatched bar is the exporter as it was before D3, on the same track: it put the mesh's joints about nine centimetres from where every joint instrument scored them.

Delivered GLB vs its own FK, performer 1

visuals.title: D3: a body we built, recovered exactly through the whole delivery
visuals.plain: Synthetic truth is the reference. Six bodies with every bone length, span and spine segment drawn independently, posed, solved, exported and read back. The hatched bar is the same body arriving canonical downstream, which is what shipped before D3.

visuals.title: D3: the rig's shoulder span, fixed rig against the performer's own
visuals.plain: Limb lengths measured from our own capture are the reference. The fixed rig was 540 mm across the shoulders; the delivered body is now each performer's own width.

visuals.title: How far each body's limb lengths are from the performer's own
visuals.plain: Limb lengths measured from our own capture are the reference. A body fitted to the performer should sit well below our one-size rig.

visuals.title: D3: where the delivered rig lands on our own capture, before and after
visuals.plain: Our own capture is the reference, root-relative. Before: the fixed rig. After: the rig sized to the performer, which is now what ships.

visuals.title: Distance from MAMMA's joints, 15 body joints
visuals.plain: MAMMA's joints are the reference, at zero. Our raw capture, and the same capture driving a parametric body, on identical frames.

visuals.title: What the retarget costs on the arms, and how much sizing the rig recovers
visuals.plain: Our own capture is the reference. The last bar per performer is the converter's own floor, a round trip on a body built to the rig's proportions; nothing above it is proportions.

visuals.title: D2: where the arm root lands on the delivered character, before and after
visuals.plain: Our own capture is the reference, root-relative. Before: the collarbone aimed from a made-up point on the spine. After: aimed from the joint it pivots about, with the rig's hips placed on the captured hips. The legs are shown to prove they did not move.

visuals.title: D2: the converter's own round trip on a canonical body, arms
visuals.plain: A body built to the rig's proportions is the reference, so the right answer is zero. Before: the known clavicle cost. The hatched bar is the best any constant on the spine could do, which never reaches the band. After: the rig's own geometry, no constant.

visuals.title: D2: the same converter on MAMMA's own joints, arms
visuals.plain: MAMMA's rigid skeleton fed through the converter and scored against itself: a separate reference from our capture, never on one axis with it. MAMMA reports here and selects nothing.

visuals.title: What D2 cost and D2c gave back: frames where a collarbone or arm joint turns faster than a human joint can
visuals.plain: A physical ceiling of 800 degrees per second is the reference. Aiming the collarbone from a pivot only 100 to 160 mm from its landmark turns landmark wander into angle; the hatched bar is the collarbone fix alone. D2c rejects frames a collarbone cannot reach at that speed and re-solves the arm below. MAMMA's collarbones through the same measure never approach the ceiling. The median step is unchanged, which is the lever and not this step's to fix.

visuals.title: D2c on synthetic truth: collarbone error on a body whose true motion is known, worst frames
visuals.plain: Exact synthetic truth is the reference: our own motion through the real cameras with the detector's measured noise injected, so the right answer is known. The 95th percentile of the collarbone's error is shown; the median is unchanged because the reject touches 2 percent of frames. The hatched bar is a heavy smoother, which scores better here and destroys 64 percent of true peak speed, which is why it is the wrong answer.

rungs.title: Hands
rungs.status: measured: 36.5 mm held-out, degenerate hands rejected; the shipped hand is under-smoothed

visuals.title: The hand fit scored on a camera it never saw, per hand
visuals.plain: No truth on disk: each hand is fitted on three cameras and scored on the fourth, then rotated. MAMMA's own hand through the same protocol sits above ours because of a skeleton convention gap, so this chart proves the gate rejects a frozen hand; it does not rank us against MAMMA.

visuals.title: Fingertip jitter: how much the fingers shake frame to frame
visuals.plain: The thrash figure. Beside each hand is the part of the shake that is the whole wrist moving rather than the fingers, which is a floor under it. MAMMA's fingertips shake about 0.2 mm on this scale and sit on a different skeleton, so they are not drawn.

rungs.title: Head orientation
rungs.status: measured; thorax window now 9 (synthetic truth, 2026-09-02): medians improved on both performers, p95 mixed, the gate's own floor rose, performer 0 flipped PASS -> FAIL on p95

visuals.title: How closely the head follows MAMMA's, relative to the chest
visuals.plain: MAMMA's head in our chest frame is the reference. MAMMA's own head through our frames is the floor; a head that never moves is the wrong answer that must lose.

visuals.title: How far above the floor the head sits, once the frame's own jitter is cancelled
visuals.plain: Our head's worst-case (p95) disagreement minus MAMMA's own head scored through the same frame, on identical bootstrap draws. This is the figure a change to the chest frame cannot move, and the one ground truth would turn into a target.

rungs.title: Feet, toes and ground contact
rungs.status: measured against MAMMA; a constant 17-24 deg inward toe offset on every foot

visuals.title: How closely each foot follows MAMMA's, once the constant offset is removed
visuals.plain: MAMMA's foot direction in the shin frame is the reference. Its own foot through our frames is the floor; a foot welded to the shin is the wrong answer that must lose. The constant offset is reported separately: our toes point about twenty degrees inward.

rungs.title: Mesh and delivered skeleton -- the end-to-end rung, deliberately last
rungs.status: measured; faces the right way since 2026-09-02 (D1: the naming mirror relabelled at five sites)

visuals.title: D3: the delivered character against MAMMA's joints, before and after
visuals.plain: MAMMA's joints are the reference, at zero; agreement with an instrument, not accuracy. Before: the fixed rig. After: the performer's own body. The aqua bar replays the new rotations on the old fixed rig, which is what a consumer that ignored the skeleton would show.

visuals.title: D2: the delivered character against MAMMA's joints, arms and legs kept apart
visuals.plain: MAMMA's joints are the reference, in absolute world coordinates, so unlike the root-relative charts this one can see where the character actually stands. Agreement with another instrument, not accuracy. The arms improve a lot and the legs a little, as written down before the numbers.

visuals.title: The delivered character against MAMMA's joints, end to end
visuals.plain: MAMMA's joints are the reference, at zero, the same reference as the pose rung. The gap between the fixed rig and the sized rig is the body; the rest is everything above compounded.

visuals.title: Which way the delivered character faces, part by part
visuals.plain: +1 means a part points the same way the performer does in the footage; -1 means exactly the opposite way. Since the 2026-09-02 fix every part points with the performer; before it the pelvis, chest, head and the mesh's own nose read -0.9 to -1.0 while the feet were right. The hatched bar, our capture turned 180 degrees, is what backwards looks like on this scale. MAMMA's independent reading of the performers is the ceiling a head can reach.
